subject.title: fix(openai): allow RFC 2544 fake-IP range for Realtime session requests

question: Should OpenClaw accept a hostname-scoped fake-IP SSRF exception for OpenAI Realtime secret requests, and should the helper be exposed through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime`?
rationale: The implementation is narrow, but it intentionally changes a security boundary and expands public Plugin SDK API surface, which requires maintainer intent rather than automated cleanup.

options.title: Accept after repair
options.body: Approve the scoped SSRF and SDK tradeoff, then require the shared-test mock repair, a rebase, refreshed SDK budgets, and focused API/test proof before merge.

options.title: Keep policy local
options.body: Use the same `SsrFPolicy` shape inside the OpenAI plugin and avoid exporting another public Plugin SDK helper.

options.title: Decline the exception
options.body: Leave fake-IP proxy users on DNS/proxy exclusions or disabled fake-IP mode for Realtime until a broader networking policy is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept after repair
recommendation.body: Approve the scoped SSRF and SDK tradeoff, then require the shared-test mock repair, a rebase, refreshed SDK budgets, and focused API/test proof before merge.
